rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to tune selectivity in either direction.

Change only gradient duration to test whether the central critical pairs respond to a shallower slope. The last peak should remain near or below 10 minutes, leaving room to gain resolution without a time penalty.

The shallower gradient improved the limiting pair substantially, leaving only R = 1.20 to fix. Raising temperature while keeping the gradient unchanged tests selectivity tuning and should preserve the last-peak time below 10 minutes.

The central peak pattern suggests the critical pair may have reversed elution order between 40 and 50 C. A further 5 C increase tests whether it separates again on the other side of that crossover while retaining adequate separation elsewhere and finishing below 10 minutes.

After the temperature-induced order reversal, a slightly steeper gradient may widen the remaining critical pair rather than compress it. Shortening to 12 minutes tests this while monitoring the narrower gap between peaks 4 and 5 and reducing the last-peak time.

Injection 5 achieved the maximum CRF, so retain it as the benchmark and test a shorter gradient. This probes the speed limit for full resolution, with the gap between peaks 4 and 5 most likely to become limiting.

Return to the successful 12-minute duration and raise the starting organic fraction one step to trim the weak-solvent portion. This tests whether the last peak can elute sooner while preserving both critical separations; injection 5 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

Retain injection 5 as the maximum-score method and explore a faster selectivity regime. A steeper gradient at 60 C may carry the limiting middle pair through an elution-order crossover and restore separation on the other side.

Test the cooler selectivity regime against injection 1 at the same gradient slope. Cooling may open the central critical pair enough to permit a shorter fully resolved method, while the broad gradient should still elute all compounds below 10 minutes.

Refine the maximum-score method with a slightly shallower gradient to improve the marginal separation between peaks 4 and 5. The other critical pair should remain near baseline resolution, and the last peak should still elute comfortably below 10 minutes.

Test a trimmed, shorter gradient that balances the selectivity effects of starting organic fraction and slope. This targets full resolution near the successful region while retaining injection 5 as the maximum-score benchmark.

Preserve injection 5's successful gradient slope exactly while removing the unused high-organic tail. The last peak previously eluted near 0.57 organic fraction, so ending at 0.80 should retain full resolution with a shorter programmed gradient.

Make the gradient shallower than injection 11 to restore the limiting middle separation while retaining the slightly stronger start. This targets a maximum-score method with more resolution margin than injection 5 and a last peak comfortably below 10 minutes.

With maximum CRF already secured, test a faster high-temperature regime using a stronger start to shift the crossed middle pair farther apart. The slightly shallower slope than injection 8 may improve its other limiting gap, while the first peaks will be monitored for excessive loss of retention.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to test whether the remaining crossed middle pair opens beyond R = 1.5. Injection 14 already resolves every other pair, but the early pair must be monitored as its retention decreases.

Return to the successful 55 C selectivity regime and use a shallower gradient to compensate for the stronger start. This tests whether both middle critical pairs can gain resolution margin while the earliest peaks remain retained and the last peak stays below 10 minutes.

Use a slope midway between injections 13 and 17 to balance their two critical separations. This should retain maximum CRF with a last peak near 8 minutes and slightly more resolution margin than the fastest confirmed method.
